title: Fix the quantifier in the Frobenius specialization lemma
would_establish: The exact valid specialization statement needed by A36 Lemma 7.5, with a clear distinction between an arbitrary generization in a normal ambient scheme and the generic point of a normal integral base.
known_scope: The literal arbitrary-point version of Lemma 7.8 is refuted in the dossier by a rank-one Frobenius module on a smooth ambient scheme and a nonsplit nodal specialization. The generic-point repair is proved using the finite étale fixed locus and its henselian finite part; Stacks0BTN,04GK and 02LP supply the precise ingredients.
first_concrete_step: Inspect the wording and insertions on 36:026–027, then follow the use of 7.8 in7.5. Record whether the intended reduction changes the normalization or special residue field.
achievable_output: A corrected companion proposition, a dependence diagram for 7.5, and an explicit statement of the residue-field obstruction. The established counterexample is a test for the proposed wording; the task does not seek to prove the refuted statement.

title: Type the local Verdier pairing and its global comparison
would_establish: One map-by-map construction of the local correspondence pairing, its pushforward through the support counit, and its precise relation to integration of the global trace.
known_scope: Perfect evaluation and the published Lefschetz–Verdier formalism are available. The manuscript’s local existence, local isomorphism and global trace compatibility are separate assertions; finite Tor dimension alone does not supply every constructibility or boundedness condition.
first_concrete_step: Write the four objects, both Hom factors and each adjunction arrow in the 33:144→146→148→160 sequence. Compare that single typed diagram with original SGA5 III§4, fixing shifts, supports and Koszul signs.
achievable_output: A verified diagram and a hypothesis table for one correspondence. The local and global assertions remain separately labelled, even though their source entries have been consolidated.

title: State trace additivity with its precise enhancement data
would_establish: A companion statement distinguishing strict cone-compatible endomorphisms, arbitrary morphisms of distinguished triangles, and intrinsic trace of a perfect object presented by an unbounded complex.
known_scope: The elementary supertrace proofs and counterexamples are already checked in the dossier. They determine the necessary diagram data, but they do not decide the ink of the deleted boundedness qualification or turn every triangle morphism into a compatible cone endomorphism.
first_concrete_step: Collate the boundedness marks and the exact published additivity statement. In one fixed cone model, identify the homotopies or enhancement that make the endomorphism diagram compatible.
achievable_output: A minimal correct theorem, one counterexample explaining each omitted condition, and a clear account of resolution independence. This is a finite commentary task, not a request for a new general trace theory.

title: Resolve internal Ext, support polygons and top-edge conventions
would_establish: One fully indexed local-to-global Ext spectral sequence with the correct sheaf/global convention, support dimension, and top-edge assertion.
known_scope: The finite-field and purity counterexamples in the dossier show that the missing sheaf mark and dimension normalization change the theorem. ILO XVII6.2 is an exact modern comparator; it does not identify a guessed polygon before the original indices are fixed.
first_concrete_step: Check the Ext mark, codimension word, spectral-sequence page and total-degree indices on 33:172–180. Then compute the support region and edge map for a single clearly specified bounded complex.
achievable_output: A corrected support diagram and a short list of hypotheses for the uniform bound and localization duality. The distinct constructible-approximation question is reserved for D16.

title: Audit the Néron and p-adic implication diagrams
few_hour_reach: High for one implication; medium for the full audit
would_establish: A source-based hypothesis table for the editorial Néron limit objections, the arithmetic orthogonality proof, and the good-reduction/inertia implications at ell different from p and at ell=p.
known_scope: The dossier has a good-reduction ordinary elliptic example with nonsplit p-adic inertia representation. Original SGA7 IX 5.12–5.13 distinguishes the prime-to-p criterion from Barsotti–Tate extension. Completion base change, arbitrary limits, torsion subgroup closure and orthogonal-complement equality have different assumptions.
first_concrete_step: Inspect the p-adic parenthesis on 34:068–069 and match the two directions separately to IX 5.11–5.13. Then attach the 36:004 Remark 2.6(a) objection to the relevant IX 2.4–2.6 proof step without assuming identical draft numbering or scope.
achievable_output: One complete implication diagram and a separate ledger for completion, finite étale lifting, henselianity, excellence and finite residue fields. The categorical torsion-extension question and the independent completion question must remain visible within that ledger.

title: Identify the finite invariant-cycle sequence and its vertical torsion obstruction
would_establish: An exact statement of the amended finite invariant-cycle sequence, including its Brauer term and p-primary topology, together with the obstruction to replacing the torsion Picard component P^tau by P^0 in higher dimension.
known_scope: Raynaud1970 supplies the divisor/Picard ingredients and the curve comparison; §6.4.1 uses P^tau. In the curve case P^tau=P^0. The earlier CRAS announcements and every amended draft case have not been matched completely. The vertical kernel is different from the later component-group cokernel.
first_concrete_step: Retrieve the original CRAS264 pages 941–943 and 1001–1004, identify the cited theorem3 and proposition7(ii), and write their hypothesis matrix. Use that matrix to specify one regular proper higher-dimensional degeneration whose vertical torsion can be followed into P^tau/P^0.
achievable_output: A concordance for the finite sequence and a precisely defined obstruction group; a small example is a reasonable next output. The bibliographic matching and the higher-dimensional example are distinct work packages within the same vertical-Picard problem.

title: Separate whole-space trace variation from the nonconiveau conclusion
would_establish: A precise fate statement for the strong Hasse–Witt whole-space trace claim, and a separate complete finite-field deduction of the nonconiveau conclusion from stable-rank growth.
known_scope: The weaker invariant-subspace assertion does not imply the strong theorem or its every-residue corollary. Katz, SGA7 XXI 1.4, proves nonnilpotence; Koblitz1975 I§5 Theorem 2 gives stable-rank growth. The dossier’s finite-field deduction retains the fixed ambient zeta factors. None of these is the original every-whole-space-trace statement.
first_concrete_step: Fix one family, base field and whole-space quantifier. Trace that exact assertion through the primary bibliography, while writing the determinant factorization for the stable-rank argument with each ambient factor displayed.
achievable_output: Two explicitly separate propositions: the established finite-field implication with its scope, and an exact statement of what remains unidentified in the stronger trace-distribution claim. A short run should not promise the general converse from eigenvalue divisibility to correspondences.

title: Complete the categorical gluing theorem for biextensions
would_establish: An equivalence of the actual Picard groupoids described on 36:048–050: a restricted biextension plus all compatible finite torsion pairings, with the one-variable and two-variable hypotheses stated correctly.
known_scope: The quotient tensor vanishing is proved. SGA7 VII 2.7 and VIII 1–2 give the long exact and Tor/pairing machinery, but no complete proof at the draft’s full generality was certified. The bounded-torsion example shows that retaining only the Tate pairing can lose information.
first_concrete_step: Write the long exact Biext sequence, including automorphisms, and identify the obstruction and ambiguity maps. Construct a candidate quasi-inverse before iterating in the second variable.
achievable_output: Either a fully faithful, essentially surjective reconstruction with explicit morphisms or a sharply identified missing hypothesis. Agreement of isomorphism classes alone is insufficient; the finite-level system remains part of the data.

title: Test faithful flatness for the actual H+D families
would_establish: Whether the specified inverse and divided-derivative axioms force the ambient formal-series ring to be faithfully flat over the chosen family, when the constant extension is faithfully flat.
known_scope: The polynomial-family counterexample refutes a D-only interpretation. It does not satisfy the additional H axiom and therefore does not answer the H+D question. Standard Weierstrass systems impose further hypotheses that cannot be imported without checking them.
first_concrete_step: Inspect the ambiguous axiom letter d. Fix a coherent local intermediate ring satisfying the full family axioms, and check locality, unit reflection and flatness one at a time.
achievable_output: A proved subclass, a genuine full-family counterexample, or a precise missing-axiom statement. The unrestricted theorem should not be promised within a few hours.

title: Separate the compatibility and semisimplicity conjectures
would_establish: A theorem-by-theorem status table separating degreewise inertia trace, alternating trace, Weil–Deligne compatibility, a common rational form, geometric semisimplicity and weight–monodromy.
known_scope: The negative-trace example already refutes the literal nonnegativity assertion. Geometric semisimplicity is different from arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity. The inspected Kato/Lu–Zheng results and the 2026 hyperkähler preprint have explicit scopes and do not settle every cell of the manuscript’s broad formulations.
first_concrete_step: For each claim on 34:033–036, index smoothness, properness, residue field, coefficient prime, degree and semisimplification. Attach one exact primary theorem or an explicit remaining gap to each cell.
achievable_output: A reliable compatibility table with separate rational-form and motivic-extension questions. The task updates precise formulations, not a single universal status label for all compatibility problems.

title: Reduce one weight-piece independence question to correspondence ranks
few_hour_reach: Low for the general conjecture; medium for one reduction
would_establish: The exact conditional implication from algebraic correspondence ranks to ell-independence for one chosen normal-crossing weight complex.
known_scope: The dossier records van Dobben de Bruyn’s equivalence theorem. Purity separates weights but does not determine the ranks of all restriction or Gysin maps. The general independence assertion remains conjectural at the stated scope.
first_concrete_step: Choose one differential d1 or d2, identify the algebraic correspondence that would represent it, and list the precise standard-conjecture or rank-independence input required.
achievable_output: A finite conditional theorem or a known-case reduction with every dependency named. The expected few-hour result is a rigorous reduction, not a solution of the general independence conjecture.

title: Fix the residue and d2 signs in a normal-crossing complex
would_establish: A coherent sign convention connecting the local Kummer-residue induction with the restriction/Gysin differentials in one proper normal-crossing spectral sequence.
known_scope: The local admitted square can be checked after fixing cup order and the Gysin convention. Coefficients must extend across the ambient strict-local scheme; the broader interpretation has a counterexample. Weight separation allows d2 and gives E3 degeneration, not automatic E2 degeneration. The motivic rank compatibility remains a separate assertion.
first_concrete_step: Choose a two-component proper model. Write the support and open-complement localization triangles over the same cochain algebra, compute the r=2 residue square, and then identify the resulting d2 with its duality sign.
achievable_output: One local compatibility lemma and one completely signed spectral-sequence example. These are two distinct calculations sharing the same boundary convention; neither is replaced by a broad appeal to purity.

title: Join the four-space cone diagram to the degree-and-depth conventions
few_hour_reach: Very high for a companion diagram
would_establish: A single typed account of the local spaces, the two different localization triangles, the delayed cone comparison, and the specialization degree boundaries.
known_scope: The manuscript uses Phi_man=RΦ[−1]. Its punctured-fibre step needs vanishing throughout that punctured fibre, not merely at the removed point. Localization, codimension-one purity, derived inertia invariants and the checked degree bounds supply the ingredients; part(b) and a boundary sign still need coherent maps.
first_concrete_step: Put both localization triangles in one fixed cone model. Record the rectified-depth convention and the lower and upper specialization endpoints, then compare the four-space diagram with Illusie2003’s variation diagram.
achievable_output: A definitive degree/sign table and one verified cone diagram, including the later isolated-lci degree n+1 statement. The uniform-support hypothesis must be visible at the arrow where it is used.

title: Recover the sharp geometric-depth comparison
would_establish: The exact localization and flat-local-map inequality for geometric depth defined by the minimum number of generators of a regular-presentation ideal, including the role of the residue extension.
known_scope: SGA2 XIV 5 and Illusie’s finite-type relative version are identified. The invariant is neither ordinary depth nor a definition using arithmetic rank. The full all-noetherian wording and removal of the extra residue-field hypothesis were not matched.
first_concrete_step: Express the invariant through the first two terms of the cotangent complex for a regular presentation. Follow every use of separability or formal smoothness in the flat-map comparison.
achievable_output: A sharp hypothesis statement, with one proved special case or obstruction for removing the residue-extension condition. The documentary ambiguity must be resolved before a purported general proof is attempted.

title: Find the valid boundary of the infinite-root dimension bound
few_hour_reach: High for a precise boundary; medium for a new case
would_establish: A narrower correct dimension-reduction statement for the Kummer root tower, with excellence, regularity or geometric normal-crossing hypotheses made explicit.
known_scope: The arbitrary noetherian assertion is false by the dossier’s Orgogozo example and Cartan–Leray deduction. The regular-parameter Kummer computation and geometric local results provide positive cases. The already-refuted unrestricted statement is not an open conjecture.
first_concrete_step: Compare the dimension-two nonexcellent example, the simultaneous-root calculation, Gabber affine Lefschetz and the known geometric-local setting in one hypothesis table.
achievable_output: An exact boundary theorem or primary-source match, and a well-posed remaining case. A few hours can clarify which assumption fails; they do not justify promising a new unrestricted theorem.

title: Test constructible approximation with injective stalks
would_establish: A precise positive result or counterexample for writing a sheaf with injective stalks as a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves with injective stalks.
known_scope: The arrow-category example distinguishes injectivity of stalks from injectivity of the sheaf. It does not settle the actual approximation question. No exact match in the searched literature was found, which is not evidence that the question is presently open.
first_concrete_step: Fix a noetherian scheme and a finite self-injective coefficient ring. Model one finite stratification by a diagram category and test both the stalk condition and the transition maps in the proposed filtered system.
achievable_output: A verified finite-stratification theorem or a counterexample meeting the actual hypotheses. The first run should produce a useful test case and an exact statement, rather than extrapolating from stalkwise injectivity alone.

title: Trace the publication of the arithmetic coinvariant exposé
would_establish: A publication concordance for the finite geometric abelian coinvariants theorem and its almost-all-primes conclusion, preserving the generic-curve reduction and boundary Tate twist.
known_scope: The dossier checks the finite-Jacobian proof, the dual invariants/coinvariants distinction and the open-curve localization sequence. C198 has been corrected to retain the generic parameter and valuation-control step. The printed SGA7 II exposé is a different text; numbering alone does not prove identity.
first_concrete_step: Trace citations backwards from SGA7 I and the arithmetic fundamental-group literature. Match normality, geometric connectedness, finite generation, the finite-field reduction and the almost-all-primes quantifier one statement at a time.
achievable_output: A dated source concordance with exact theorem numbers and a complete dependency map. The task should not redo a weakened curve proof that drops the generic-parameter or inertia-image requirement.

title: Repair the solvable-monodromy and constant-part reductions
would_establish: A correct chain from solvable or unipotent Tate action to the appropriate constant-part or CM conclusion, with each field extension, radicial isogeny and torus quotient stated exactly.
known_scope: The claimed arbitrary-radical isogeny has a counterexample. The CM quadratic twist shows that a general finite cover cannot be replaced by a constant-field extension. C203–204 remain classC because the exact application of Grothendieck1966 Proposition 4.4 is not fully verified; this is not a declaration of new mathematical openness. The nilpotent Frobenius-density argument is a distinct checked special case.
first_concrete_step: Obtain Proposition 4.4 in full and align its hypotheses with the geometric abelian-scheme setup. Then rewrite the radical argument using the correct torus quotient and list which steps require a cover, a constants extension or a radicial isogeny.
achievable_output: A qualified implication diagram, an exact publication match where available, and an explicit list of the still-missing adaptations. Preserve the finite-level rigidity and CM steps as separate sublemmas.

title: Realize the ordinary-factor lifting counterexample
would_establish: A fully specified algebraic family completing the page’s proposed counterexample to lifting the largest ordinary abelian subvariety.
known_scope: If the generic abelian surface is geometrically simple, a positive-dimensional proper special abelian factor cannot lift as an abelian subvariety. The missing point is an exact family with the ordinary/nonordinary product as special fibre and the required generic simplicity. Formal and p-divisible subgroups are different objects.
first_concrete_step: State the intended meaning of a lift, then locate a primary deformation or moduli theorem for that precise ordinary-times-nonordinary special fibre. Check that its hypotheses yield an algebraic abelian scheme with geometrically simple generic fibre.
achievable_output: An explicit family or a complete cited existence argument, followed by the already-understood simplicity obstruction. A short run should not upgrade the original sketch before the family is checked.

title: Compute the weighted component-pairing comparison
would_establish: The integral comparison between the weighted divisor lattice and Grothendieck’s geometric component pairing in one concrete relative-curve model.
known_scope: The abstract discriminant construction is checked. Residue weights can make the apparent dual lattice have nontrivial index. Bosch–Lorenzini4.6–4.7 gives a qualified Jacobian comparison and perfectness conditions; those hypotheses must remain attached to the geometric claim.
first_concrete_step: Choose a regular curve model with nontrivial residue degrees delta_i. Compute the actual integral dual lattice, the intersection map, the two finite groups and the induced comparison pairing.
achievable_output: A completely worked example showing the finite index defect or proving its absence under the chosen hypotheses. This is a tractable calculation, without a promise of a new general perfectness theorem.

title: Recover the early pairing equality and its normalization
few_hour_reach: High once the two formulas are found
would_establish: The exact equality, sign and Tate-twist convention between the two pairings questioned in the early SGA7 editorial leaves.
known_scope: Finite perfectness does not determine an overall sign. Deligne10.2.4 and SGA7 VIII 2.3 provide transition and transposition comparisons, but the two formulas referred to as A.M. and “yours” are absent. The later weighted curve pairing in D20 is related evidence, not an established identification of those early maps.
first_concrete_step: Recover both draft formulas, the operation R and the one-factor versus two-factor transition. Normalize them on one elliptic-curve example before proving the categorical comparison.
achievable_output: A finite-level equality with explicit conventions and a verified passage to the Tate limit. If one formula remains unidentified, the output should be a precise archival locator and an unresolved comparison, not an inferred equality.

title: Write the complete rigidity-to-NS continuation
few_hour_reach: High for a companion; medium for the unfinished lift
would_establish: One coherent statement across36:052 and 054–058 covering group-Hom versus pointed-map vanishing, primitive torsors, biextensions, the symmetric NS defect and the proposed doubled Picard splitting.
known_scope: The one-variable primitive-torsor result and formal kernel injection are proved under universal rigidity. The continuation imposes extra additivity and an explicit special-case equivalence. Original SGA7 VII 2.9 and VIII 4.10–4.14 supply the qualified geometric comparisons. The quadratic sign alarm and unfinished canonical lift still need their own treatment.
first_concrete_step: Join parts a, b, c with the same coefficient group and base-change convention. State which hypothesis makes each forgetful functor fully faithful, then identify the diagonal lift and verify its homomorphism and canonicity conditions.
achievable_output: An annotated theorem chain and a separate last proposition for the doubled lift. The consolidated problem MP-SA13-134 retains that unresolved substep within the continuous NS object.

title: Reconstruct the finite-to-adic trace passage
would_establish: The exact compatible system, uniform amplitude, finite-generation and inverse-limit hypotheses needed by the adic trace construction.
known_scope: The finite-projective matrix calculation is checked. SGA5 V–VI provides the historical finite-to-adic framework and explicitly does not construct a full modern adic derived category. An elementary congruence alone does not supply the required uniform derived bounds.
first_concrete_step: Write the finite-level system used on 33:128 and follow it through one proper-pushforward or compact-support example, recording every use of uniform Tor amplitude and limit exactness.
achievable_output: A complete statement for one geometric system and a table of the missing conditions in the broader wording. This remains distinct from D24’s uniform descent of group-scheme data and D8’s retention of finite pairing information.

title: Find one model controlling an entire Tate tower
would_establish: A justified passage from levelwise finite descent to a single finite amount of model data controlling all torsion levels in the stated adic setup.
known_scope: The quantifier gap between “for every level there exists an extension” and “one extension works for every level” is explicit. SGA7 IX 2.6(a) handles its own arithmetic setting. Detecting a finite torsion point after a finite extension does not create a compatible rational division tower.
first_concrete_step: List the finite-presentation objects used for every nu and identify one group scheme, multiplication map, filtration or biextension that determines them all. Check its descent hypotheses once, before iterating the torsion level.
achievable_output: A uniformity lemma with exact assumptions or a precisely located failure. The task concerns uniform model data, not a claim that every finite pairing is recoverable from a Tate-module pairing.

title: Prove one named projection or Künneth coherence square
would_establish: One resolution-independent base-change or composition compatibility for the projection and Künneth maps that the manuscript marks for checking.
known_scope: SGA4 XVII5.2.9 and 5.4.3 gives the canonical maps; some auxiliary compatibility diagrams are left to the reader. The already-established general framework does not identify which exact omitted square is intended on the leaf.
first_concrete_step: Choose one square on 33:114–116 and follow every arrow through the original bounded resolutions, including the comparison maps between two choices.
achievable_output: A complete proof of that named square and a reusable convention statement. A few hours can settle one compatibility; the task is not an unspecified reconstruction of the six-functor formalism.

title: Formulate the singular Picard–torsor comparison correctly
would_establish: A precise singular or relative H1(X, A)–Picard/Ext statement, with the site, Picard component, base terms and internal/global distinction fixed.
known_scope: The nodal infinite-order abelian torsor and the real Brauer class rule out two unrestricted interpretations. Raynaud6.2.1 proves a finite locally free relative Cartier-dual Picard formula. That theorem does not automatically give the manuscript’s unspecified absolute abelian-torsor comparison.
first_concrete_step: Choose one pointed nodal curve over an algebraically closed field and write the normalization and derived Picard sequences. Specify the relative site and retain the base-cohomology terms before comparing Ext groups.
achievable_output: A valid special-case theorem or a diagram exhibiting the missing correction term. The direct-limit Q/Z correction and the distinction among Pic^0, Pic^tau and the full Picard functor must remain explicit.

title: Recover the functors in the higher-duality programme
would_establish: One well-posed finite bounded adjunction or duality comparison behind the handwritten f_! and higher-Picard formulas.
known_scope: The current symbols leave the site, variance, dualizing object and degree conventions underdetermined. Finite-free exchange and split evaluation are checked special cases. The cancelled divisor argument only produces a Weil divisor without additional Cartier hypotheses; derived filtrations and differentials cannot be replaced by an unexplained direct sum.
first_concrete_step: Locate the missing definitions in the adjacent archive material, including33:166–167. Fix one f_! comparison and write its edge maps and competing terms before asking for a theorem.
achievable_output: A typed formulation with a short verified special case and a list of documentary dependencies. Broad derived-category terminology is not itself a resolution of the programme.

title: Specify the noetherian-base cohomological-dimension hope
would_establish: A hypothesis table separating noetherianity, finite dimension, finite type, excellence and coefficient invertibility in the proposed relative cohomological-dimension bound.
known_scope: The specified Gabber–Illusie finite-dimensional prime-to-characteristic theorem is an established comparator. It does not settle the broader literal wording. The later nonexcellent examples show why changing the base hypotheses can be decisive.
first_concrete_step: Compare the quantifiers on 33:110 with the exact ILO statement and one counterexample from the depth or infinite-root leaves. Identify the smallest formulation that the printed theorem actually proves.
achievable_output: A precise statement of the established range and one sharply formulated remaining case. Keep this relative-bound question distinct from the particular Kummer-tower dimension reduction in D15.

title: Match the nonabelian depth proposal to local Lefschetz theorems
would_establish: The exact boundary between the trait theorem for low-degree or prime-to-p torsor specialization and the proposed arbitrary excellent local-base extension.
known_scope: Raynaud1974 and Orgogozo2003 have precise base and codimension restrictions. The manuscript’s geometric resolution and local Lefschetz dependencies are stronger than a generic subject-level reference to a modern theorem.
first_concrete_step: Make a table with base, codimension, coefficient group, degree and geometric-depth assumption for the manuscript and each exact comparison theorem. Resolve which ambient space carries the singular-locus codimension.
achievable_output: A theorem-by-theorem concordance and a well-defined broader proposal. A short run can locate the exact remaining hypothesis without claiming to settle all excellent-base nonabelian specialization.

title: State the arithmetic model-group Tate theorem completely
would_establish: A complete proposition realizing the manuscript’s Tate endomorphism expectation in the arithmetic-model representation category, including normal-base extension and removal of finite component obstructions.
known_scope: The arithmetic Tate Hom theorem and Gajda–Petersen’s normal-base lemma settle the qualified model setup. Moret-Bailly XII2.4–2.5 gives the positive-characteristic provenance. Replacing the arithmetic model system by the ordinary geometric fundamental group would change the statement.
first_concrete_step: Define the filtered Hom category for a normal qcqs base and check that an individual commuting matrix and the needed geometric data descend to a finite stage. Identify the later stage where the relevant component quotient vanishes.
achievable_output: A complete exact-scope theorem and proof with the publication/circulation distinctions preserved. This is a completion of settled mathematics in the manuscript’s notation, not a new Tate conjecture.

title: Separate analytic, algebraic and profinite reconstruction
would_establish: An exact comparison statement replacing the conflicting recovery sentence and the claim that both arithmetic Lie dimensions are always infinite.
known_scope: The dossier already checks fibre-functor reconstruction, recovery of the profinite component quotient, the obstruction to rational points meeting every component, and the finite-field example with analytic dimension one and algebraic dimensions unbounded.
first_concrete_step: Translate the categories and natural arrows on 34:185–188 into one diagram. Distinguish an isomorphism of pro-objects, equality of Lie algebras, openness of an analytic image and equality with all rational points.
achievable_output: A corrected diagram and concise propositions explaining the two counterexamples. The task should preserve the role of the fibre functor and avoid replacing the actual Zariski-envelope density by a false general component-group criterion.

title: Prove BCH membership from the exact flow axioms
few_hour_reach: High for a test case; medium for the full argument
would_establish: Whether the manuscript’s permitted flows and substitutions are sufficient to keep the BCH group law and induced homomorphisms inside the chosen A-family.
known_scope: The ambient formal BCH theorem is established. The leaf’s Ado reduction is unfinished, and an ambient matrix-group construction does not itself prove membership in A. Formal evaluation at1 is not automatically permitted.
first_concrete_step: Work through a nilpotent matrix example with a multigrading and only allowed substitutions. Then isolate the exact closure statement needed to pass through the nonnilpotent Ado construction.
achievable_output: A complete low-nilpotence case and a precise list of remaining A-membership obligations. The initial deliverable is bounded and testable even if the full axiom implication needs additional assumptions.

title: Test restricted-class Frobenius and quotient effectivity
would_establish: When the first integrals of an involutive distribution and the effective quotient of its relation remain inside A, rather than only existing in the ambient formal category.
known_scope: The characteristic-zero constant-rank formal Frobenius theorem is established. The manuscript treats A-effectivity as an additional closure axiom. The rank-one flow comparison does not by itself prove the higher-rank restricted-class assertion.
first_concrete_step: Specify a rank-two integrable distribution in an explicitly generated A-family. Construct local first integrals and check their chart transitions against the permitted substitutions and quotient criterion.
achievable_output: A verified restricted-class example, a sufficient closure lemma, or a counterexample satisfying all initial axioms. Preserve the distinction between existence of an ambient quotient and membership of its maps in A.

title: Compare minimal inverse-closed families with henselization
would_establish: The exact relation between closure under formal inverses and the algebraic power-series henselization, including the limits of a converse for arbitrary families.
known_scope: The henselian-pair criteria and ambient inverse theorem are checked. Henselianity solves algebraic implicit systems; it does not automatically imply closure under inverses of every chosen formal series. The minimal algebraic power-series example is a specific valid family.
first_concrete_step: Fix the field and augmentation. Construct finite stages of the minimal H-closed family and compare them with explicit étale neighborhoods of the polynomial local ring.
achievable_output: A precise minimality statement or a finite-stage obstruction to the proposed converse. The expected result is a useful formulation and test case, not an unqualified identification of all henselian families.

title: Resolve the integral saturation qualifier in monodromy
would_establish: The precise integral filtration intended by the word pure or saturated, beyond the established rational unipotence bound.
known_scope: The q+1 nilpotence theorem is established. A canonical spectral filtration, its rationalization and the intersections of rational subspaces with an integral lattice are different constructions. Saturation is not automatic in an arbitrary spectral sequence with torsion.
first_concrete_step: Inspect the adjective on the scan and identify which of those filtrations is meant. Test that definition on a torsion example before seeking a geometric saturation theorem.
achievable_output: An exact convention and either a verified restricted statement or an explicit extra hypothesis. The task does not reopen the already-established broad monodromy theorem.

title: Descend A-coordinates and principal parts for projective modules
would_establish: Coordinate-independent A-structures for finite projective modules, their principal parts and the associated induced smooth structures.
known_scope: Affine chart calculations work under the relevant H+D hypotheses. Finite projectives require transition and descent arguments; arbitrary finite modules may be singular and need a larger category. The local calculations alone do not certify global coordinate independence.
first_concrete_step: Choose a rank-two projective module on a two-open cover. Write its transition cocycle and verify that the Hasse-derivative and principal-parts constructions respect it; then check one induced smooth completion.
achievable_output: A transition-cocycle lemma and a worked projective example. Keep the singular finite-module extension outside the initial theorem while recording it as a separate later enlargement.

title: Audit the rational-point interpolation threshold
would_establish: A correct explicit degree threshold, or a precisely stated limitation of the proposed bound, for sections with a prescribed finite number of rational points.
known_scope: Broad existence follows from finite-point interpolation after a finite field extension. The norm forms are valid and may be geometrically reducible. The sharper same-degree construction and coprime-product improvement require separate control of selected sets and disjoint rational zero loci.
first_concrete_step: Reconstruct the actual finite split complete intersection and its selected subset. Check N≤r*d1^n, the final zero-set notation, and the dependence of the field extension and degree on N before optimizing the degree arithmetic.
achievable_output: A verified bound in one fixed dimension or a concrete obstruction to the written threshold. Preserve the distinction between singular-section existence and a smooth-section assertion.

title: Determine the geometric content of the multiplicity-gcd insertion
few_hour_reach: High for the source question; uncertain for realization
would_establish: Whether a hidden geometric constraint justifies the written product of gcds, or whether it is a genuinely false insertion in the multiplicity/index formula.
